title: Education
grammar_topic: Present Perfect; contraste del Present Perfect con otros tiempos
can_do: Puede hablar de experiencias y acciones pasadas relevantes para el presente y hablar de educacion/trabajo

grammar_explanation.core_rule: El Present Perfect (have/has + participio pasado) conecta el pasado con el presente: se usa para experiencias de vida o acciones pasadas cuyo resultado importa AHORA, sin decir exactamente cuando pasaron. Si dices CUANDO exactamente (yesterday, last year, in 2020), tienes que usar Past Simple, no Present Perfect.

structure_notes.label: negativo
structure_notes.example: I haven't applied for that job yet.

structure_notes.label: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
structure_notes.explanation: Present Perfect = sin tiempo especifico / relevante ahora. Past Simple = tiempo especifico mencionado.
structure_notes.example: I have graduated (en algun momento) vs. I graduated in 2020 (tiempo especifico).

examples: I have worked in marketing for three years.
She hasn't started her new job yet.
He graduated last year. (NO 'he has graduated last year')
exceptions: 'Ever' y 'never' se usan para hablar de experiencia general en la vida, casi siempre con Present Perfect: 'Have you ever worked in a restaurant?' — nunca con Past Simple con este sentido.
'Just', 'already' y 'yet' acompañan frecuentemente al Present Perfect: 'I have just finished my degree' (recien), 'I haven't finished yet' (todavia no).
grammar_explanation.common_mistake: Usar Present Perfect con una fecha o tiempo especifico: 'I have graduated in 2020' es incorrecto — debe ser 'I graduated in 2020' (Past Simple).

grammar_practice.q: I ___ not started my new job yet.

reading.title: From Classroom to Career
reading.text:
Laura has always been interested in technology. She studied computer science at university and graduated three years ago. Since then, she has worked for two different companies, and she has learned a lot about the software industry.

Her first job was an internship at a small startup. She hasn't forgotten how nervous she felt on her first day. 'I had never worked in a real company before,' she says. 'I had a lot to learn.' During that internship, she gained practical experience that her university courses hadn't fully prepared her for.

After six months, she applied for a full-time position at a larger company. She has been there for over two years now, and she has already received one promotion. 'I've learned that qualifications on paper aren't everything,' she explains. 'Employers also want to see that you can apply what you know.'

Laura's advice for students who haven't started their careers yet is simple: get as much practical experience as possible, even before graduating. 'I did an internship every summer during university,' she says. 'That experience has helped me more than any single class.' She also recommends applying for scholarships and taking on projects outside of regular coursework whenever possible.

questions.q: What did Laura study at university?
How long ago did Laura graduate?
According to Laura, what matters besides qualifications on paper?
options: Being able to apply what you know
questions.answer: Being able to apply what you know

questions.q: What can we infer about the value Laura places on internships?
options: She thinks they are a waste of time
She believes they were more valuable than her classes
She thinks only summer internships count
questions.answer: She believes they were more valuable than her classes

listening.title: A Career Interview
listening.transcript:
Host: So, tell me about your career so far. Have you always worked in education?
Guest: Not always, actually. I've had a few different jobs. I started in sales right after I graduated.
Host: Interesting! What made you switch to teaching?
Guest: Well, I hadn't really enjoyed sales, and I've always liked helping people learn. So I did a teaching certificate a few years later.
Host: Have you ever regretted the change?
Guest: Never. I've been teaching for six years now, and I've never been happier professionally.
Host: That's great to hear. Have you thought about what's next for you?
Guest: Yes, actually. I've just applied for a coordinator position at my school. I haven't heard back yet, but I'm hopeful.

questions.q: What was the guest's first job after graduating?
Why did the guest switch careers?
options: They didn't enjoy sales and liked helping people learn
questions.answer: They didn't enjoy sales and liked helping people learn

questions.q: How long has the guest been teaching?
Has the guest heard back about the coordinator position?
What can we infer about the guest's feelings about teaching?
options: They are very satisfied with the change
They want to go back to sales
They are unsure about their career
questions.answer: They are very satisfied with the change

writing.prompt: Escribe un correo informal (80-120 palabras) a un amigo contándole sobre tu experiencia educativa o laboral. Usa el Present Perfect para hablar de experiencias generales y el Past Simple para hechos con tiempo especifico. Usa al menos 3 palabras de la lista de vocabulario.
writing.example_answer: Hi Andres, I hope you're doing well! I wanted to tell you some news. I've finally finished my degree — I graduated last month, actually! It's been a long journey. I've also applied for a few jobs already, and I have an interview next week for an entry-level position at a marketing company. I've never worked in marketing before, but I did an internship in a similar area last year, so I have some experience. I haven't heard back from the other companies yet, but I'm staying positive. How about you? Have you started your new job yet? Write back soon!

rubric.descripcion: Cuenta una experiencia educativa/laboral con formato de correo informal claro.
Usa ambos tiempos correctamente segun corresponda (experiencia general vs. tiempo especifico).
Usa al menos 3 palabras de la lista de vocabulario de forma natural.
Sigue la estructura de un correo informal (saludo, cuerpo, despedida) con ideas conectadas.
